page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra processor family, specifically utilizing Neoverse-N1 cores. It features 2 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, which equates to approximately 1.95 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 40 GB NVMe SSD. The instance runs under the QEMU hypervisor and does not include any dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest performance across most workloads. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the average tier at 1821.28, but multi-core performance drops to the bottom 25% with a score of 3610.67. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, measuring 131.92 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 25.88 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Real-world application benchmarks show weak to poor results, including a static web serving throughput of 2.46 GB/sec and a Redis SET throughput of 2.58 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation and low-tier resource footprint, the cax11 is positioned as a highly cost-efficient entry-level option for non-critical workloads. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU model and limited memory capacity, which restrict its capability under sustained multi-threaded stress. However, for lightweight tasks, the inclusion of fast NVMe SSD storage provides responsive local I/O despite the lower processing and memory bandwidth limits.

This server is best suited for lightweight, non-resource-intensive applications. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, simple automation scripts, and lightweight database operations that do not require high concurrency or massive memory footprints.
